source.title: U-REPA: Aligning Diffusion U-Nets to ViTs
source.authors: Yuchuan Tian; Hanting Chen; Mengyu Zheng; Yuchen Liang; Chao Xu; Yunhe Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures tokenwise cosine alignment during training and argues that this metric is limited for U-Net-to-ViT alignment; it proposes a relational manifold loss as a refinement.
record.gate_note: The paper intentionally trains models with representation-alignment objectives, so those results do not show that alignment arises naturally as models scale or become more capable. The reported generation-quality metrics and layer/upscaling ablations are downstream method outcomes, not direct measurements of representational similarity, and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper trains diffusion models with an explicit loss that forces alignment to frozen ViT (DINOv2) features, then reports generation quality (FID/IS). The only similarity numbers (Fig. 3) track cosine similarity that the REPA loss itself is maximizing. They show how well an induced alignment is reached, not whether independently trained models converge. The paper's argument against tokenwise cosine concerns it as a training loss, not as a measure of convergence, and it reports no comparison of similarity across metrics, neighbours or inputs. Under the rules, inducing the behaviour on purpose is not a test, so this is T4: the finding is used as a tool and only the method's performance is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that aligning diffusion U-Nets to ViT encoders is hindered by different block roles, spatial mismatch and feature-space gaps, which make strict tokenwise cosine alignment suboptimal. U-REPA addresses these with middle-stage alignment, MLP-then-upsample and a relational manifold loss. They report faster convergence, with FID 1.41 at 400 epochs versus REPA's 1.42 at 800.
record.recipe_differences: The paper adapts REPA for diffusion U-Nets and adds post-MLP upsampling and a manifold loss; it does not test natural convergence across independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported tokenwise cosine trajectory differs between SiT-L/2 and SiT↓-L/2; the authors also argue that strict tokenwise alignment is less suitable for the U-Net/ViT feature-space gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Under an explicit REPA alignment loss to DINOv2 features, the U-Net-style SiT↓-L/2 plateaus at tokenwise cosine ~0.60 vs ~0.63 for isotropic SiT-L/2 (Fig. 3). The authors attribute this to architectural and feature-space gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How closely a diffusion backbone can be forced to match a pretrained ViT's tokenwise features under an alignment loss depends on architectural similarity to the ViT (isotropic transformer > U-Net).

record.problems: The relevant similarity evidence is limited to tokenwise cosine measurements for two model variants. It does not compare representation-similarity measurements under the proposed manifold metric, and it does not test scale, performance trends, or out-of-distribution inputs.
record.rows_left_out: Generation-quality results in Tables 3–15 and the layer, dimension, and upscaling ablations report FID or IS rather than representation similarity; excluded under the row criteria.

untested.parts: Alignment of independently trained models as scale or capability grows; not measured.
Vision–language alignment on paired data; not studied.
Seed convergence of representations. Seeds 0–2 are reported only for FID (Tab. 14), not for representations.
Mapping or stitching between independently trained models with little loss; the MLP projector is trained jointly under the alignment loss and is not evaluated as a map.
Shared interpretable features or circuits; not studied.
Dependence of measured convergence on metric, settings or inputs. Only tokenwise cosine is measured; the manifold metric is used as a loss but never reported as a similarity measure.
Incompleteness or plateau of natural alignment and its causes. The plateau observed concerns induced alignment only.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tranche (T5) and its V6 limits_scope label should be dropped. All similarity evidence comes from models explicitly trained to align, so it shows induced, not emergent, alignment. The authors' critique of cosine similarity targets it as a training objective, not as a convergence-measurement methodology. The FID ablations (layer depth, upscaling, w) are method performance and were correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Whether alignment between independently trained models increases with model size or capability.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions, and whether it rises with both models' capability.
Convergence across random seeds in networks of the same architecture.
Whether representations can be transferred or mapped between models with little loss, including through a linear map, stitching, relative representations, or without paired data.
Recurrence of shared interpretable features or circuits across models.

The paper measures tokenwise cosine similarity and argues for a relational alternative, but does not report similarity results under both metrics. It does not vary neighbour count or input distribution, or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, and whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete across a scale sweep.

rows.subject: SiT-L/2
rows.operation_detail: Measured average tokenwise cosine similarity to ViT features during training.
rows.measure: Average tokenwise cosine similarity to ViT features
rows.note: The paper reports this trajectory as the comparison for the U-Net-based model; it does not report uncertainty for the similarity value.
rows.check: SiT-L/2 is trained with the REPA loss, which directly maximizes tokenwise cosine similarity to ViT features. The ~0.63 value is an optimization outcome of induced alignment, not natural convergence. It has no bearing on V6, since only one metric is reported and the version's metric or data dependence is never measured.

rows.subject: SiT↓-L/2
rows.operation_detail: Measured average tokenwise cosine similarity to ViT features during training.
rows.measure: Average tokenwise cosine similarity to ViT features
rows.note: The paper says early improvement is slightly faster, but later progress stagnates and the plateau is below the SiT-L/2 result.
rows.check: SiT↓-L/2 is also trained with the explicit alignment loss; the 0.60 plateau is induced alignment. Reading this row as a plateau under V7 would be wrong, because the alignment is forced by the objective. No alternative metric is measured, so it does not bear on V6 either.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: U-Net-based SiT↓-L/2 under tokenwise cosine measurement
reader_labels.reason: Tokenwise cosine similarity plateaus at 0.60 for SiT↓-L/2, below the around 0.63 reached by SiT-L/2; the authors describe limitations of this alignment metric for the U-Net/ViT feature-space gap (r1, r2).
